=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple images clearly show leaves radiating from a single node in groups of four)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are densely packed in whorls along the stem)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3.	Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (leaves consist of a single blade without distinct leaflets)
    4.	Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5.	Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6.	Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7.	Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins appear smooth, though some edges show irregular damage)
    8.	Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaves are longer than wide and taper towards the tip)
    9.	Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (leaf tips come to a distinct, sharp point)
    10.	Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (leaf base tapers down to the petiole forming a wedge shape)
    11.	Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single main midrib with lateral veins branching off)
    12.	Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible (lateral veins are distinct and curve towards the leaf margin)
    13.	Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): glabrous and dull (surface appears smooth without hairs and lacks significant sheen)
    14.	Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on the leaf surface)
    15.	Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are very short, appearing almost sessile)
    16.	Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear rounded and cylindrical)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17.	Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stems appear thin, green, and soft)
    18.	Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stems appear smooth)
    19.	Stem color: green (stems are green, similar to the leaves)
    20.	Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (stems appear smooth without distinct ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21.	Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are clearly visible at the leaf nodes)
    22.	Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex is visible)
    23.	Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus is visible at the base of the petioles)
    24.	Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils are present)
F. Notes: Several leaves exhibit holes and missing sections along the margins. Small, greenish-yellow flower buds are visible in the center of the terminal whorls.
